findings.title: Runner crashes in envelope (a) and in the note's freq_per_stratum: 0 fallback, after all burst compute is spent and after the sealed primary metrics are written
findings.detail: The E002.yaml header presents envelope (a) as differing ONLY in n_layouts 30, freq_per_stratum 0, check_strata [u_shaped:6], cpu_hours_est 52 and timeout_min 600. Design note §4 also recommends `freq_per_stratum: 0` for (b) if (b) must stay under 180 CPU-h. With freq_per_stratum 0, sec_idx is empty, so `si = np.array(sec_idx)` is a float64 array and `l2_20[si]` raises IndexError (e002_ranking.py line 539). This happens after every L2 solve has finished and after spearman_rho_Lloop, mape_Lloop and top_decile_recall have been computed on the sample. The result.json then has status 'error' and contains the sealed-sample primary values. All compute (~52 CPU-h) is lost, and a rerun would re-evaluate data that has already been seen (F5 hazard; max_evaluations 3). Envelope (a) is also the only option inside O001's frozen budget (cpu_hours: 60). Neither the DoD smoke (sec_idx = [0]) nor the author's harness (n = 30 but freq_per_stratum left at 1) exercises this path.
findings.evidence: Reviewer harness: full-mode main(False) at the envelope-(a) config, dev seed 424242, synthetic L2 records, run_tasks monkeypatched. Output: `RAISED IndexError arrays used as indices must be of integer (or boolean) type`, traceback at `l2s20 = l2_20[si]`, status error, all 7 sanity checks passed, primary metrics already reported. Isolated check: `np.array(sorted([])).dtype` is float64, and indexing with it raises IndexError.
findings.suggested_check: Use `np.array(sec_idx, dtype=int)` (or guard on len(si)), then rerun the full-mode harness with freq_per_stratum 0 and check_strata of length 1.

findings.title: l2_reference_valid validates solvers.l2, not solvers.l2_layout, the solver that produces every E002 reference value
findings.detail: The in-run reference check re-solves E001's C1 with moduleforge.solvers.l2 (annulus/harmonic wires, l2.solve). E002's L2 values come from solvers.l2_layout. That module has its own filament-bundle wire model, rod/box corrections, precorrected-FFT wire-grid operator, lattice cell_fill, bilinear contacts and die shorts, and shares only l2_core with l2. A defect specific to l2_layout cannot fail this sanity check. The l2_layout-vs-l2 link on C1 (0.5 %) exists only as a unit test (test_c1_layout_internals_vs_l2_solve_same_refinement), not in-run. Provenance pinning (source_sha256 over l2_layout + l2_core) partly mitigates this.
findings.evidence: l2_layout.py docstring and imports (only `from moduleforge.solvers import l2_core as core`); e002_ranking.child() 'c1' branch calls e1.l2_solve(l2, ...); tests/unit/solvers/test_l2_layout.py:265.
findings.suggested_check: Add an in-run C1 (or straight-trace DC closed form) solved through the l2_layout path, as the unit test already does.

findings.title: The draft's default envelope (b) at 158 CPU-h is 2.6x O001's frozen budget (cpu_hours: 60)
findings.detail: The note frames (a) <= 60 and (b) <= 180 as founder choices and recommends (b). It does not state that the objective's own frozen budget is 60 CPU-h, so registering the draft as written needs a budget change on top of the envelope choice. I could not see the T0076 packet to check whether 180 CPU-h was authorised there.
findings.suggested_check: Founder confirms the budget, or the draft carries (a) once the blocker above is fixed.

findings.title: The bias band assumes d1 < 0 for every k*-1 layout
findings.detail: b_hi_layout uses r_max and b_lo_layout uses r_min for all k*-1 layouts. That is correct only when -d1 > 0. For a layout whose 0.5 to 0.25 mm step is positive, the extremes swap, and the 'rigorous' band may not contain that layout's own [r_min, r_max] interval. All dev layouts had d1 < 0, so this is an edge case.
findings.suggested_check: Take min/max over both r_min and r_max for each layout.

findings.title: 'l2_converged' passes while the estimated residual bias at k* exceeds its own 1 % tolerance
findings.detail: The gate tests the k* to k*+1 step (dev: 0.49-0.73 %), but the geometric extrapolation puts L2(k*) 1.3-1.9 % above its lateral limit. 'Converged' therefore means 'step < 1 %', not 'error < 1 %'. A4 reads the uncorrected mape_Lloop, and the bias inflates it when L1 < L2. The note discloses this and adds l2corr and refbound metrics plus a founder decision point. The 'rigorous' refbound is rigorous only given a band built from 3 three-level layouts, a constant-ratio assumption and an ad hoc 0.5-point margin.
findings.evidence: Design note §1 and §0.2; E002.yaml l2_converged and mape_Lloop_refbound descriptions.

findings.title: The smoke DoD cannot catch full-mode defects; 'complete' only means every declared sanity check was reported
findings.detail: ExperimentRun sets status 'complete' when all declared sanity checks are reported, whether or not they passed and whether or not the runner returned 1. The E002 smoke runs kb = 0 with no k*-1 level and one stratum, so strata selection, d1/contraction, k*-1 bias, F4 and the die correlations are untested by the DoD. Only the author's synthetic harness covers them, and it missed the blocker. Also, check_pairs_concordant_frac (declared) is not emitted when fewer than 2 layouts are checked (envelope a).

independent_checks_performed: Ran `uv run mfos exp check E002` and `uv run mfos exp check E003`: both pass. Ran `uv run ruff check` on both runners: clean.
Ran the E003 smoke DoD myself: status complete, single_thread_enforced passed (CPU/wall 0.999), p50 16.8 ms, p90 22.7 ms, 6-die p50 23.3 ms. This matches the note's ~18 ms uncontended figure.

Reviewer harness, full-mode main(False) at the envelope-(a) config (n 30, freq_per_stratum 0, check_strata [u_shaped:6]) with synthetic L2: reproduced an IndexError crash, status error, with the primary metrics already written.

Reviewer harness, envelope-(b) config at n = 30 with a per-layout varying synthetic geometric ladder L_k = T(1 + c_i 0.61^k), c_i in [0.021, 0.059]. All sanity checks passed and status was complete. The recovered contraction was 0.6100. The true beta range [0.0127, 0.0349] (computed by hand) lies inside the reported band [0.0077, 0.0392]. mape_Lloop_l2corr 0.089 is about the true MAPE vs T (~0.09) and lies inside the refbound [0.064, 0.115]. This confirms that beta = -d2/(1-r), the k*-1 extrapolation -d1 r/(1-r) and the corrected reference are implemented as derived.
Re-derived the geometric-ladder bias by hand (L_inf = L_k(1 + d2/(1-r)), hence beta = -d2/(1-r)) and reproduced the note's 1.3/1.9/1.8 % from the cost.json steps.
Checked ape_range analytically: L1/(L2(1-beta)) is monotone in beta, so the max is at an endpoint and the min is 0 iff the root 1 - L1/L2 lies in the band. The code matches.
Read mfos.stats: topk_recall defaults to lower_is_better=True (correct for inductance minimisation), mape(pred=L1, ref=L2) uses L2 as reference, and spearman uses average ranks.
Checked A5/K3 resolution: at n = 90 (k 9, w 18) A5 needs 7/9 and K3 fires at <= 4/9; at n = 30 they are 3/3 and <= 1/3, as stated.

Spot-checked the K1 power claim with the Fisher-z / Bonett-Wright variance: n = 90, rho = 0.64 gives power ~0.82; n = 30, rho = 0.48 gives ~0.81. Spot-checked P(A4) at MAPE 0.113, n = 90: about 0.19 by normal approximation, vs 0.18 reported.
Checked the cost arithmetic: 90 x 1.23 + 15 x 2 x 0.5 + 15 x 0.32 + (9.3 + 9.3 + 8.8) + 0.5 = 158 CPU-h, and k* c(d) is consistent with the cost.json values 1.02 / 0.99 / 1.45.
Checked that L1's image plane is the backside-Cu top face (peec/model.py docstring), so plane_dist_proxy is consistent with L1's physics. The note discloses the fixed-stack limitation for F3.
Traced the provenance of the L2 reference: l2_layout imports only l2_core; the C1 sanity check runs solvers.l2.
caveats: I could not run the E002 smoke DoD (`rm -rf /tmp/e002-smoke && ... --smoke`): the session's permission mode denied it. The E002 smoke result is taken from the design note and not reproduced by me. The orchestrator's deterministic checks will run it.
The T0076 task packet was not available, so I could not verify whether the 180 CPU-h envelope or the packet's 'changes (1)-(4)' authorised the deviations the note describes.
My harness used synthetic L2 records and L1 fine meshes of 2 and 1 mm only (for speed). It tests code paths and formulas, not the physics of l2_layout.
Envelope (b) as written in the draft does not hit the blocker. If the founder registers (b) unchanged and never sets freq_per_stratum 0, the runner's full-mode path ran to completion in my harness.
